title: Cap. IX Arg. 7 Sol: to reprobate is to permit by denying special grace — not to pour spiritual malice; media to death are deficient evils from us, not from God
pass_a_gloss: For to reprobate is, By denying special grace, to permit some to fall short of the end of beatitude, not by pouring in spiritual malice to drive them by force into the abyss of misery. Hither also it is added, that the media by which the predestined are led unto life are certain supernatural goods, and therefore to be sought from nowhere else than from the Fountain of good: unto God therefore predestinating it pertains to provide concerning efficacious media, by whose intervention the predestined may be saved: But the media by which the reprobate rush unto death are spiritual evils, are deficient and depraved actions: therefore they are to be sought not from the highest Good, nor from God as efficient, but from our implanted evil, and from a deficient cause. It is therefore inept and impious on account of the antecedent decree of reprobation to think that it incumbs upon God to produce in the reprobate unbelief, impenitence, and other things of that kind, by whose intervention they are damned. Finally, this also is to be known, that Unbelief, impenitence, and whatever falls under the account of sin, can be called media by which the reprobate himself procures death unto himself: But in respect of the Reprobating One they are not media effected and applied by God unto the damnation of the reprobate, but rather matter which the reprobate brings forth from himself, God foreseeing and about the same matter exercising his vindicative justice.
pass_b_english: To reprobate is, by denying special grace, to permit some to fall short of beatitude's end — not by pouring spiritual malice in to drive them by force into the abyss of misery. Add this: the media by which the predestined are led to life are supernatural goods, and so to be sought only from the Fountain of good — it belongs to God predestinating to provide efficacious media by whose intervention the predestined are saved. But the media by which the reprobate rush to death are spiritual evils — deficient, depraved acts — and so are sought not from the highest Good, nor from God as efficient, but from our implanted evil and a deficient cause. It is therefore inept and impious, because of an antecedent reprobation decree, to think God must produce in the reprobate unbelief, impenitence, and the like by which they are damned. Finally: unbelief, impenitence, and whatever counts as sin can be called media by which the reprobate himself procures his own death. But respecting the Reprobating One they are not media God effects and applies unto the reprobate's damnation — rather matter the reprobate brings forth from himself, God foreseeing and about that matter exercising his vindicative justice.
source_text: Nam reprobare est Negando gratiam specialem permittere aliquos a fine beatitudinis deficere, non infundendo malitiam spiritualem in abyssum miseriae per vim eos impellere. Huc etiam accedit, quod media quibus praedestinati ducuntur ad vitam, sunt bona quaedam supernaturalia, ac proinde non aliunde quam a Fonte boni petenda: ad Deum igitur praedestinantem pertinet providere de mediis efficacibus, quorum interventu praedestinati salventur: At media quibus reprobati in mortem ruunt, sunt mala spiritualia, sunt actiones deficientes et depravatae: ergo non a summo Bono, neque a Deo efficiente, sed ab infito nostro malo, et a causa deficiente petantur. Ineptum igitur et impium est propter antecedaneum reprobationis decretum putare, id Deo incumbere, ut producat in reprobatis infidelitatem, impoenitentiam, et id genus alia, quorum interventu damnentur. Denique, et illud sciendum est, Infidelitatem, impoenitentiam, et quicquid peccati rationem subit, dici posse media quibus ipse reprobatus sibi mortem procurat: Sed respectu Reprobantis non sunt media a Deo effecta et adhibita ad damnationem reprobati, sed potius materia quam ex se parit reprobatus, Deo praevidente et circa eandem materiam justitiam suam vindicativam exercente.
